resources.string: Added native wallpaper-service reconnect self-healing to prevent broken status-bar contrast after wallpaper updates, unified Monet rendering and cross-surface sync, rebuilt Perfect Icons on direct Git sync, fixed Bilibili 9.21.0+ startup stalls, added HyperOS Home 9263 and Themes 11.6.0.0 compatibility, and refined MIUIX Glass interactions.

string-array.name: release_notes_1_18_0_changes
string-array.item: Automatic status-bar contrast recovery after wallpaper updates\nAdded native wallpaper-service reconnect self-healing in HyperOS Home: if updating or restarting the system Wallpaper app triggers the OEM 10-second bind timeout or binding-death race, KeiHome automatically retries with backoff and restores wallpaper listeners without restarting Home. The Status bar color inversion tool now displays self-healing status, live listener count, full Home and Wallpaper versions, root-cause notes, and one-tap diagnostic copy.

Unified Monet icon rendering, completion detail, and native hardening\nUnified Monet rendering, antialiased masking, and MAML parity across icon sources; improved handling of 3-tone masks, multi-color monochrome layers, foreign MAML roots, and static animating icons; restored layered completion detail and uncovered-app coverage while preserving Telegram aliases. Native hooks now include hardened memory guards, single-pass tint scanning, clean policy-server teardown, and exact native capability bitmask reporting.

Consistent Monet sync and clean OFF restoration across system surfaces\nFixed cross-process palette races, stale pre-existing status-bar and notification-center icons, Share sheet async callback and ViewHolder recycling races, and original-icon restoration in Sidebar and Settings when turning Monet off. Toggling Monet on or off now stays symmetric across Home, status bar, notification center, Recents, and the HyperOS Share sheet.

Hardened Perfect Icons Git sync and rebuilt theme packaging pipeline\nRetired the legacy HTTP ZIP archive path in favor of hardened direct GitHub Git sync with connection reuse, adaptive batching, retries, and resumable staging, eliminating Git I/O storms and mask cache poisoning. Introduced a typed theme IR with a single-pass overlay pipeline and unified the coverage-gated icon mask contract across splash and surface renderers.

Bilibili 9.21.0+ adaptation and startup ANR fix\nHardened Compose footer discovery, ABI binding, and edge-to-edge gesture bar synchronization for Bilibili 9.21.0+. Moved DexKit resolution off the startup path and added a versioned persistent profile cache, eliminating long stalls and crashes on the Bilibili launch screen.

HyperOS Home 9263 and Themes 11.6.0.0 compatibility\nUpdated native structure matching to support Monet selection on HyperOS Home RELEASE-8.01.02.9263-261013-11192009-R, and hardened local icon-pack lookup and import resolution for HyperOS Themes 11.6.0.0.

Upgraded MIUIX Glass transitions and title-side help popups\nUpdated to the MIUIX e636bd6c snapshot with single-pass backdrop sampling and unified OS4 bottom-bar stow/restore transitions between main and detail screens. Refined title-side info buttons to use compact Glass popups for concise hints and escalate to bottom sheets only for longer explanations, with cleaner alignment and typography.

resources.string: This update changes the native launcher library (.so). Other scopes refresh automatically via API 102 hot reload, so you normally do not need to reboot your phone — just restart System Launcher once and return Home to load the new native capabilities (wallpaper reconnect self-healing and HyperOS Home 9263 support). Reboot the device only if the new native build does not load after restarting Launcher. To apply Monet and Perfect Icons packaging improvements, update or regenerate your icon pack and apply it again.

Fixed Lock screen editor wallpaper bleed-through, refreshed notifications after static light/dark icon swaps, hardened API 102 hot reload, surfaced full icon pack names and version timelines, and refreshed MIUIX Glass screens and interactions across the app.

string-array.name: release_notes_1_17_0_changes
string-array.item: No desktop bleed-through in Lock screen customization\nHyperOS dark-mode wallpaper dimming now applies an opaque black dim layer over the wallpaper surface instead of lowering its transparency. Entering the Lock screen style editor no longer lets the home screen show through the preview.

Notifications update after static light/dark icon swaps\nWhen static light/dark icon switching swaps the icon archive, SystemUI reopens the updated theme resources and clears cached native app icons so the status bar and notification center reflect the new appearance.

More reliable API 102 hot reload\nHardened old-generation retirement, cleanup, and provider retry handoff after in-place updates so hooked processes reload more reliably without manual restarts, and fixed runtime status freshness timers to expire accurately.

Full icon pack names, versions, and applied times\nStatus now shows the full active icon pack name without truncation alongside its source type, coverage, applied time, version, and update state. Icon Packs and pack cards distinguish generated and imported packs, display build or applied times instead of missing-version placeholders, and stamp newly generated or exported packs with KeiHome-linked version numbers.

More reliable dark cutouts and icon pack rendering\nPerfect Icons now derives dark textures for eligible isolated animated cutouts while preserving alpha masks, keeps Fixed dark for ordinary icons visible on the Perfect Icons page, and preserves adaptive bounds when rendering quiet layer snapshots. Built-in icon store assets are also verified to remain seekable in release packages.

Refreshed Status, About, and MIUIX Glass interactions\nUpgraded to the MIUIX bc1024d7 snapshot with unified Glass top bars, sticky tabs, GlassCard sheets, small-window safe insets, and Smooth corners. Rebuilt the Status cards and Runtime/Monet detail sheets for clean single-screen readability, polished About with hero scroll fade and idle shader pausing, and added OS4 spring motion across switches, previews, and lists.

Redesigned Cache management and Theme settings\nUpgraded Cache management with an interactive 3D storage cylinder, scrub leader line, category storage hub, inline preview-memory clear, and budget presets. Refined Theme settings appearance preview cards and added color-coded OS4 icon badges across navigation hubs.

Rebuilt layered icon studio, fallback, and tool screens\nRewrote the Custom static layered icon editor into an OS4 Glass studio sheet with a squircle-clipped live preview, and rebuilt Icon fallback with a visual resolution pipeline. Refreshed Custom and Preserved icons, Log settings, Perfect connection and resource sheets, App scale live preview, Apple pack, Icon mask, and Recommended mappings.
Cleaner switch help sheets\nMoved lengthy switch conditions and activation notes into dedicated help sheets next to each switch title so explanations stay readable even when a switch is disabled.

Clearer Release notes layout\nCollapsed release cards now preview each version’s summary, and the installed version is marked with a Current badge. Expanded entries use numbered badges, stronger title/body contrast, tinted footnote callouts, a synchronized scrollbar, and a clearer empty state for Unread.

resources.string: No native launcher libraries changed in this release, so updates normally apply through API 102 hot reload. To get the icon generation and version metadata improvements, update or regenerate your icon pack and apply it again.
Create layered icons, see the temperature on the Weather icon again, and adjust dark mode from a single page.

string-array.name: release_notes_1_16_0_changes
string-array.item: Build your own layered icons\nIn Perfect Icons → Custom, choose an app and add a background and a foreground. The editor saves them as 0.png and 1.png, shows the saved icon in Custom, and includes it when you generate the pack.

Use static icon artwork for light and dark mode\nAn optional setting prepares separate light and dark artwork for eligible static icons. Home swaps them when the system appearance changes and refreshes affected icons together. Supported dynamic icons keep their animations. Thanks to @jizizr for the static icon switching and batched refresh contributions.

Weather shows the temperature again\nPerfect Icons restores the original Xiaomi Weather animation and temperature on Home. The status bar, notification center, and Recents use the available weather artwork from the same layers.

Dark mode settings in one place\nOpen Home → Dark mode settings to find the system dark style, low-brightness contrast, wallpaper dimming and presets, launch overlay, and status bar color inversion. On supported HyperOS builds, choose from three dark styles for compatible system surfaces and select HyperOS or ColorOS wallpaper dimming.

More consistent gesture bar colors\nWhen Match bottom bar color is enabled for a supported app, the gesture area follows more Hongguo tabs and playback screens, and matches the background of the Douyin comments panel.

Rounder launch icons and more reliable icon packs\nLaunch icon completion follows the theme outline when an app such as Candysign falls back to an opaque square icon. Imported ColorOS packs keep compact dark-mode resources, and third-party Telegram clients retain their own launch icons. Built-in ColorOS icon tabs also keep the Glass header as you switch styles.
Smoother Home editing with dynamic icons\nHome batches cleanup of dynamic icon resources to reduce stalls when opening the page thumbnail view with a large pack applied.

Find the guide, license, and credits more easily\nOpen Release notes to revisit the setup guide. The KeiHome license is now under Open-source notices, and About has a contributor acknowledgments page.

resources.string: This update changes the native launcher library. Restart your device after updating, then unlock it and return to Home. To get generated icon changes, update or regenerate the icon pack and apply it again.
Choose wallpaper presets for light and dark mode, dim wallpapers in dark mode, and find new options for icon packs and app appearance.

string-array.name: release_notes_1_15_0_changes
string-array.item: Different wallpapers for light and dark mode\nIn Home → Appearance → Wallpaper presets by appearance, choose a System Personalization preset for each mode. HyperOS applies its Home and Lock screen appearance when the system switches modes. Either mode can keep the current preset.

Separate dimming for the Home and Lock screens\nTurn on Dim wallpaper in Dark mode to set each strength separately. Compare the original and dimmed previews, then tap the slider track or drag to adjust. A live wallpaper shared by both screens switches strength when you lock or unlock.

Separate app appearance and palette settings\nIn Settings → Theme settings, choose a light or dark appearance and an app palette independently. Display effects are on the same page. About now uses Glass cards and reveals the title as you scroll.

More original icon layers\nConverting compatible Hyper packs preserves more layered artwork, including supported clock, calendar and weather effects. In Perfect Icons, the optional Fixed dark for ordinary icons setting uses the dark image in both modes for eligible ordinary icons.

Clearer dark icons\nIn KeiHome extra icons, Key Attestation keeps its keyhole and checkmark, VPN Hotspot keeps its signal arcs and key shading, and Fileyan’s ring stands out against its dark background.

Less work when opening Weather\nPerfect Icons uses the original static icon for weather icons that query an external provider, avoiding synchronous waits in the launcher. Weather data in the app and its widget still updates, and other supported animations such as the clock and calendar are preserved.

Notification icons follow appearance and icon pack changes\nThe status bar and notification center refresh app icons after a light or dark mode switch or an icon pack change, including notifications already on screen.

Launch icons and Dock glass fixes\nWith launch icon completion enabled and the default icon theme selected, eligible splash screens use matching HyperOS app artwork where available, fixing some square or mismatched icons. Dock Soft Glass restores its material after the launcher restarts.
Less repeated work during Home icon refreshes\nWhen an app changes, the launcher refreshes its icons and shortcuts without scanning all apps. Theme refreshes also skip redundant icon archive reads.
Glass sheets and search controls\nBottom sheets use updated Glass motion on open, close and settle. Search fields use a consistent clear button so you can start a new query right away.

resources.string: Wallpaper features require the System Framework scope. Presets depend on HyperOS support. Update or regenerate and apply your icon pack to use the icon improvements.
Adjust the Dock glass spacing, generate leaner icon packs, and find previews, updates, and application controls more easily.

string-array.name: release_notes_1_14_0_changes
string-array.item: Dock side padding and icon centering\nWith Dock glass enabled, adjust the gap between the outer icons and the glass edges. 0 dp keeps the default side spacing. The glass fits the available width while icons and touch targets stay in place. Icons are vertically centered in the glass with launcher labels shown or hidden.

Less dynamic work for generated icon packs\nGeneration and conversion omit redundant dynamic selectors for ordinary icons with identical light and dark artwork, reducing work during launcher transitions. Distinct light and dark artwork, authored clocks and calendars, live Monet colors, and resources needed for system compatibility are preserved. Large packs also require less repeated decoding, compression, and memory during preparation.

Optional lower-cost ordinary icon path\nPerfect Icons now offers a default-off Fixed dark for ordinary icons option under light/dark adaptation. Eligible ordinary icons can use a selected dark PNG directly, while authored clocks, calendars, weather, dynamic layers, and Monet resources remain intact. The automatic option keeps system-following behavior. Regenerate and apply the pack after changing the option.

Recover from import problems\nThe generated ZIP is kept if preparation for system import fails, so you can try again. If Themes takes longer to process a large pack, you can check the result of the original import.

Apply manually in full-screen Themes\nEnable Manual application in Themes in icon pack settings to open an imported pack in full screen and tap Apply. If Themes no longer has the local record, KeiHome asks you to update or reimport the pack and avoids opening a different one. Themes decides whether the pack can be applied. Incompatible packs may be rejected or display incorrect icons.

Bottom tabs for icon packs\nSwitch between generation, resource management, and icon preview in Perfect Icons. Matched icons and custom mappings are now tabs in the Apple icon pack. Built-in ColorOS style thumbnails and light and dark previews are visible again. Matched icons can be filtered directly by All, System apps, or User apps, with counts in the filters and bottom tab.

Enable KeiHome dark icons per app\nOpen KeiHome extra icons under Icon completion and fallback to find supported apps such as Scene, MT Manager, and Xiaomi Community. Compare the current pack icon with the KeiHome dark icon, enable the ones you want, then update and apply the pack. The recommended mapping can use the Weibo icon for Weibo Lite when the pack has no dedicated Lite icon.

Improved dark icons in Perfect Icons\nDark generation for eligible two-color artwork rebuilds the edges of the mark to reduce light halos from the original background. Some bright brand icons retain their brand colors on a dark background. Light icons stay as authored.

Separate tabs for Monet colors and installation\nOpen Custom colors, Palette details, and Install and update from the bottom bar. The two color cards start expanded and remember their own state. Switching color styles clears the previous apply confirmation and keeps the missing-color help out of view while the new palette is calculated. Install and update groups icon appearance, fallback coloring, full-bleed padding, and ColorOS Inspiration installation. Compatible icons from other packs can also use coloring and padding, including coloring for some native layer pairs without flat aliases. Fallback coloring prefers existing masks and can preserve light or low-contrast details from supported foreground layers. Update or regenerate as prompted, then apply the icon pack to see the changes on the launcher.

WeChat cold-start icon completion\nWith Fill missing launch icons enabled, eligible plain system splash screens can display the current theme icon on a WeChat cold start. The original app icon is used when the theme has no match. WeChat still displays its own splash artwork after the system screen.

Gesture settings card stays visible while scrolling\nThe status title, badges, and illustration remain visible when scrolling Immersive gesture bar settings. Updated Glass top bars and tabs also improve how progressive blur and fades transition.
Clearer log export guidance\nBefore exporting App logs, KeiHome explains which issues require App logs and which require LSPosed logs. Attach both if you are unsure.

resources.string: This release updates the native launcher library. After installing, manually restart your device and unlock to the home screen. To get the icon pack generation improvements, update or regenerate the pack and apply it.
Support for the new HyperOS Home release, more reliable large icon packs, consistent icons in Recents, and a refreshed Glass interface for phones and tablets.

string-array.name: release_notes_1_13_0_changes
string-array.item: HyperOS Home 0308 and 9261 compatibility\nUpdated dynamic detection for app labels, Dock and Search materials, and Monet. App names can use system, two-line, or scrolling display where supported. Mounted icon highlights refresh when the material setting changes.

Recents icons follow the current theme\nTask cards refresh their icons after appearance or icon theme changes, including tasks already running in the background. Improved matching for Phone, Security, and Themes when their launch entries use alternate components.

Launch icons scale with the window\nTurn on Fill missing launch icons to show the applied theme icon on supported plain system splash screens. If the theme has no matching icon, the original app icon is used. Apps keep their own splash artwork and branding. The icon keeps its proportions and padding as the window expands. If you swipe Home during launch or tap the icon again while the window is closing, the icon scales with the window in either direction.

More reliable large icon packs\nProcess and verify large Monet archives in batches to reduce peak memory use. Physical-device checks covered importing and applying APK, ZIP, MTZ, built-in, and generated packs, including one with 49,252 mappings. Improved the system document picker handoff and preservation of supported layered MTZ artwork.

Clearer generation and application progress\nA centered dialog shows the current stage, overall percentage, and processed and total counts when available. Percentages advance with the work reported within each stage. On supported HyperOS devices, Themes opens in a small window for applying the pack.

More control over Monet fallback icons\nGenerate Monet artwork for eligible icons missing from the pack. An independent switch makes room around artwork that fills the canvas or reaches its edges. Recommended mappings, custom icons, and original-icon choices share the matching and rendering path.
Desktop appearance tools\nOpen Desktop tools to check wallpaper and status-bar appearance information and refresh the desktop appearance configuration if contrast becomes difficult to read.

Immersive gesture bar\nOpen Desktop → Immersive gesture bar to turn on the soft glass handle. The background shows through, and highlights at the rounded ends follow the system gesture animation. The switch takes effect immediately. With soft glass off, turn on Match bottom bar color to help the plain handle adapt more quickly when a selected app switches between light and dark pages. The handle is easier to see if you go back mid-transition. Fully close and reopen those apps after changing the color settings.

Bilibili home artwork reaches the bottom edge\nGrant the Bilibili scope in LSPosed and enable the dedicated setting to add Bilibili to the selected apps automatically. Supported home layouts extend theme artwork or a solid tab bar color into the gesture area. The status card shows the installed version and the latest result.

Glass refinements for phones and tablets\nUpdated to the MIUIX f3829d3d snapshot, with better sidebar alignment and tab layout when the interface resizes. The Glass bottom bar respects system insets on both sides of the screen, and its badges stay fully visible while dragging. Progressive blur in the top bar follows scrolling. Scrollbars have a narrower touch area, stay in sync with the top bar when dragged, and follow right-to-left layouts. The cache reminder threshold, custom log duration, and icon pack connection settings use the updated Glass input fields. The icon pack progress bar reports its value to screen readers. Wide detail pages keep grouped sidebar navigation. The first-use guide explains the icon pack workflow and links directly to Desktop tools and the immersive gesture bar.

Customize the KeiHome interface\nOpen Settings → App settings to set the interface scale from 80% to 110%, enter an exact value, or restore the 100% default. Smooth corners are on by default on supported devices. Scroll end haptics are also on by default, and both have their own switches. Your blur preference is preserved, with progressive blur as the default for new installs.

Automatic hot reload retries after an update\nAfter you install an update, KeiHome retries hot reload in the background for supported processes that are still running an older version, even if you never open KeiHome. Some LSPosed versions show only the first attempt in the notification. SystemUI also releases resources used by earlier versions of the soft glass handle across updates.

Fixed gesture bar status and icon imports after restart\nAfter a device restart, KeiHome waits for the first unlock before updating gesture bar compatibility status and checking for pending system icon imports.

resources.string: After upgrading, manually restart the device and unlock to the home screen to load the new native libraries. A restart reminder appears after you leave the upgrade notes. Launcher and gesture navigation support depend on the installed system and app builds. Reapply the icon pack after changing generation options.
More control over per-app icons, a reorganized Monet editor, smoother search and refresh, and clearer management of large icon packs.

string-array.name: release_notes_1_12_0_changes
string-array.item: Custom icons take final priority\nAssign an icon from a local pack to an app and keep it across pack switches. Custom icons override other artwork; switching to or from kept originals requires confirmation. Saved entries open an original/custom comparison before editing or removal. Reapply after changes.

Clearer scopes, previews and search\nCounted views, scope filters and search help browse apps and icon resources. Opening a preview or selection step dismisses the keyboard while keeping the query. Existing results remain visible while new matches are computed, reducing loading flicker during typing. All/Unread release notes save reading per version, separately from restart advice.

A focused Monet editor\nUse quick dropdowns on the overview, separate sheets for color source, scheme and icon preview, and subpages for custom colors and palette details. Edits stay in a draft until submitted with the single Apply colors floating action. Applying preserves the current on/off state; use the switch separately. Refresh only reads system state. The help button explains drafts, the independent Monet switch, inspiration packs, and contrast.

Better large-pack import and local application\nImproved reading, validation and system Themes handoff for large ZIP/MTZ archives and complete Perfect iOS packs, with preparation progress, cancellation and working-space checks when needed. Eligible generated archives can be reused. Fixed false rejections of supported dynamic calendars and native palette templates while retaining checks against unknown programs.

Smoother app updates and native pull refresh\nCoalesced install, update and removal events to reread affected apps, reducing repeated catalog comparisons during scrolling. Native pull refresh on relevant pages handles disabled gestures and overscroll more consistently. Refined Glass toolbar spacing and tab shadows. MIUIX icons now use Glass throughout. Grouped action menus offer direct checked sorting options and filter submenus with the current selection.

Manage icon-pack storage by category\nSee imported archive sizes and open separate MTZ/ZIP, Apple and Perfect storage controls. Preview memory, downloaded resources and generated archives have distinct cleanup actions. Keep latest generated cleans older generations after the next successful generation; manual imports remain separate.

A 20-second review before exporting App logs\nExport explains its purpose and unlocks confirmation after 20 seconds. App logs cover KeiHome UI, settings and crashes; icon, launcher and module feature issues still need LSPosed logs.

Consistent status and settings cards\nReady, warning, error and checking states use a shared bottom-right symbol, leaving more room for text and status information. Details stack on narrow screens. Removed excess space below the preserve system material effects setting while retaining error guidance and retry actions.

resources.string: After changing icon resources or rules, update or regenerate as prompted and apply the pack. Submit Monet drafts with Apply colors, which preserves the current on/off state. Importing or previewing a pack does not apply a system theme; support depends on resources and the system.
Added support for Launcher 9258, improved dynamic resolution of native structures and dependency graphs, and clarified first activation, native code updates and version restart advice.

string-array.name: release_notes_1_11_0_changes
string-array.item: Resolve launcher dependency graphs by structure\nLocate features from actual code structures and dependencies, correcting false rejections caused by code and data relocation without hardcoded version checks or fixed addresses. Checks passed for 10 version fixtures, including 9258; this still does not guarantee compatibility with every unknown version.

Launcher 9258 Selection, Monet, Dock and image recovery\nImproved structure recognition for Selection dependency graphs, Monet icon processing, Dock glass and ImageRecovery while retaining required checks. A capability stays disabled if its structure does not match or cannot be uniquely identified.

Native code updates require a system restart\nThis release includes new .so native code. After upgrading, manually restart the device, then unlock to the home screen. API 102 automatic hot reload updates only the Java part; it cannot replace native libraries already loaded in a process.

Restart advice once per version\nAfter reading the upgrade notes and returning to the main page, restart advice appears once for that version. Its confirmation button becomes available after five seconds. Confirmation only acknowledges the advice; you restart the device manually.

Open-source notices and project license\nGrouped open-source components into purpose-based subpages with global search, refreshed license readers with OS4 interactions and Glass actions, added a project-license entry in About, and added the Apache 2.0 project license. Third-party components retain their own licenses and attribution, including acknowledgements for MiuiBackGestureHook research.

Visible views and counts\nPersistent tabs cover apps, preserved icons, Apple mappings, Perfect resources and previews. Counts follow the current search and filters. Shared background grouping, smoother transitions and spaced toolbar actions remove repeated work and the redundant app summary card. Downloaded Perfect styles appear first.

All and unread release notes\nRemember reading status per version, mark one or all versions read, and remember opened notes when leaving. Fresh installs start with only the current notes unread; upgrades retain intermediate unread releases. Reading and restart acknowledgements stay independent.

Complete iOS-style pack imports\nUnify size budgets across generation, import, system handoff and theme verification. Support bounded calendar clock broadcasts, local date frames and finite refresh programs. Verified same-configuration outputs are reused without repeated rendering or ZIP creation; other archive and program checks remain.

Fixed icons across icon packs\nChoose an app, a local icon pack and its icon. Saved copies take priority across packs and remain available after source cleanup. Customization and original-icon preservation ask for confirmation when switching. Reapply the pack to activate changes. Both application pickers hide unnecessary system components by default, with an option to show them. Customized and unconfigured views include search and app-origin filters. Tap a saved choice to compare the original and custom icons before editing; first-entry guidance is available again from Help.

resources.string: First activation still requires a system restart after enabling the module and granting scopes. Skipping the guide or acknowledging advice does not replace that restart. Compatibility depends on actual launcher structures and system support; passing 10 version fixtures does not guarantee every unknown version will work.
Improved OS4 interactions and status guidance, made icon information faster to load, corrected Perfect Icons dark artwork and notification icons, and improved Apple matching and hot-reload stability.

string-array.name: release_notes_1_10_0_changes
string-array.item: Smoother OS4 search and overlays\nLeaving search editing keeps the query, filters and return position. Short explanations use glass popups beside their buttons, with improved dismissal and action handoff. View switches use segmented tabs, while long category lists can scroll horizontally. Updated Glass icons, collapsed title alignment and the top-bar fade.

Status details in dedicated sheets\nRuntime and Monet details now open in separate bottom sheets to reduce page scrolling. Initial connection, authorization and feature checks show neutral loading states instead of briefly flashing red; confirmed failures still show their warnings.

Clearer first-activation steps\nAfter first enabling and authorizing the module, guidance asks you to restart the device and unlock to the home screen. The reminder stays on Status even if you skip the guide. Ordinary updates after activation still normally use API 102 automatic hot reload.

Floating import actions and compact help\nAPK and MTZ/ZIP pages have floating import buttons with a guidance sheet. Long icon-pack instructions move into help sheets, shown once on first entry to each relevant page and available again from Help. Progress, errors and important notices stay on the page.

Faster icon information and direct navigation\nReduced repeated reads, validation and main-thread work for large app inventories and icon packs. Ready content appears progressively, and filter results are retained while loading. Status opens the current pack directly by default, falling back to the overview if its source cannot be confirmed; this shortcut can be disabled.

Keep only the latest generated pack by default\nApple and Perfect Icons each retain their latest generated version, removing older generated versions after the new pack is saved successfully. Turn this off in More settings to keep generation history. Manually imported packs are unaffected.

Improved Perfect Icons dynamic layers\nPreserved supported native dynamic layers and transparency, and improved Calendar text and light/dark updates. Corrected dark Weather cloud shape and size, plus the translucent Game Center controller outline and background residue.

Clearer dark lettering and cover images\nImproved small brand lettering on dark backgrounds while preserving brand colors and artwork. Corrected gray text edges and background residue in generated pack cover images to better match their dynamic icons.

Notification thumbnails and Super Island icons\nImproved square corners in folded notification thumbnails and icon masking in the first automatic hot-reload notice. Added support for the default application-icon path in Super Island, preserving supplied notification pictures, media artwork and custom content.

Clearer Apple matching cache and retries\nFixed successful search history appearing as a seven-day cooldown. Saved reviews and misses can be retried manually, with recent results reused from cache. Failed requests and server rate limits still require the indicated wait.

Pink-and-white icon and themed splash screens\nRestored the Kei sakura pink-and-white icon palette. Startup uses pale sakura or dark rose backgrounds and follows the saved app appearance through the transition to the main screen.

Launcher 9248 and initialization stability\nAdded support for Launcher 9248 Monet, Dock and image-recovery structures. Isolated SystemUI initialization stages, coalesced duplicate recovery work, and improved listener, cache and background-task handoff during API 102 hot reload.

Confirm before exporting App logs\nLog export now explains its purpose and requires confirmation after a five-second wait. App logs cover this app’s interface and settings issues; launcher, icon and hook issues still require LSPosed logs.

resources.string: Update or regenerate and apply your icon pack to receive artwork fixes. Results depend on resources and system support. Third-party ROM compatibility still needs validation, some folder preview issues remain unresolved, and Apple server rate limits remain in effect.

Fixed icon display across system surfaces and dynamic icon light/dark updates, improved completion controls, previews and OS4 Glass interactions, and optimized frequently used hooks and resource management.

string-array.name: release_notes_1_9_0_changes
string-array.item: Fixed square icons and edge artifacts in some apps\nUnified handling of launcher entry aliases, adaptive icons and final masks, improving inconsistent icon display across the home screen, Recents, sharing, Settings and other surfaces while preserving the alternate icons provided by apps.

Improved light/dark refresh for layered dynamic icons\nFixed dynamic icons such as Calendar staying light in notifications after the home screen had switched to dark. Improved screen refresh when asynchronously loaded icons become ready, while preserving dynamic resources and the correct date.

Previews closer to applied results\nUnified corner, transparent-edge and mask rules across app lists, icon packs and detail previews. Applied themes read the published icons; mask comparisons stay separate from pending generation settings. Moved actions such as Import and Apply to the right of previews, reducing empty space and repeated placeholders.

Keep original icons and recommended mappings\nChoose which apps keep their own icons, with search, filtering and sorting. Added a Recommended mappings page with independent controls for matching system icons by app name, sharing icons across official Telegram Play/Web/Beta channels, and built-in ColorOS Theme Store mappings. Existing adaptations and the list of apps set to keep their original icons retain priority.

Independent Perfect Icons completion\nPerfect completion is now a separate option for filling gaps in system and third-party app coverage in ColorOS and other packs. Downloaded resources are checked before enabling; HyperOS4 is recommended. System icon fallback pauses while enabled and returns to the previous choice when turned off.

Perfect Icons connection options and recovery\nAdded an optional HTTPS acceleration endpoint and System, Direct, HTTP or SOCKS modes for the Perfect Icons client, without changing device-wide proxy settings. Opening a subpage directly loads the full catalog; returning to the app refreshes local download/removal status together, with limited retries after failures. Failure and cooldown notices use a consistent OS4 card, and downloaded resources remain usable offline.

Unified OS4 Glass interactions\nFirst-time use defaults to the OS4 Glass navigation bar; iOS-like remains available in App Settings. Improved native selectors, Glass press feedback, tab bars, bottom sheets and floating toolbars. Apple mappings support multi-select management and icon inspection. Fixed overlapping content in expandable cards such as Monet, and unified list filtering, sorting and action layouts.

Remove imported icon packs individually\nLocally imported MTZ/ZIP resources can now be removed after confirmation, while keeping source files and applied themes. Lists use compact count indicators. Import, removal and resource changes refresh related pages and storage statistics.

Improved cache management and status information\nThe default cleanup reminder is fixed at 520 MB and no longer varies with Perfect Icons downloads. Added app log statistics and a link to open logs, plus explanations for cache categories. Status shows the app version prefix, and onboarding includes entries for completion, keeping original icons and recommended mappings. The guide uses an independent full-screen layout, with content scrolling smoothly behind the header and fading progressively while floating controls stay accessible.

Runtime overhead and release compatibility\nOptimized icon caching, reflection and log handling to reduce repeated work on frequent paths. Retained timely refresh, API 102 automatic hot reload and cleanup of previous module generations, while updating dependencies and improving R8 optimization and runtime entry point protection.

resources.string: Icon effects depend on resources provided by apps, icon packs and the system. After changing completion, recommended mappings, masks, the list of apps set to keep their original icons or generation scope, update or regenerate the icons and apply them. Previews alone do not change the system theme.
Rebuilt Perfect Icons resource synchronization and management, added custom masks and comparison previews, and clarified how downloads, previews and applied themes relate.

string-array.name: release_notes_1_8_0_changes
string-array.item: Selected styles with incremental updates\nPerfect Icons now uses anonymous Git synchronization. The first download obtains selected styles and shared dependencies; later updates reuse local content and download needed changes. View remote revisions and update times, and use downloaded styles offline.

Redesigned resource management\nBrowse available and downloaded styles, filter the list, update or delete individual styles, and enter selection mode for batch downloads or removal. Downloaded entries show their size and offer Update, Delete, Preview and Close. Destructive actions require confirmation.

Clearer synchronization feedback\nA temporary card shows stage, progress and elapsed time during synchronization, then disappears. Improved shared-resource size accounting, failure and interruption feedback, and local state refresh when returning to the parent page, while retaining usable resources.
Popular styles first\nNew users start with HyperOS4. Menus prioritize HyperOS4, HyperOSClassic, HyperOS3, Hyper and default, while preserving saved choices.

Custom icon masks\nAdded an Icon mask page. Automatic completion stays on by default: authored masks take priority, with HyperOS4 used when missing. Import a custom transform_config.xml or restore automatic selection, while preserving special icon configurations.

Shared preview rules and mask comparisons\nAPK, MTZ/ZIP, Perfect Icons and Apple previews share mask rendering rules. Compare real icons with original, HyperOS4 and custom masks. Applied-theme previews still read the published configuration instead of pending generation settings.

Stronger layered dynamic resource checks\nValidate dynamic entry configuration, static preview layers and animation resources while preserving valid existing formats. Incomplete resources are not treated as complete dynamic icons, reducing preview and generation errors.

Familiar interactions and timely refresh\nUnified OS4 confirmation dialogs, icon actions and resource selection toolbars. Improved return navigation, download state and preview coordination, reducing repeated work and unnecessary recomposition while retaining progress and status updates.

In-app release history and updated guide\nSettings now includes versioned release notes. Fresh installs open onboarding; a changed version prefix opens notes once. This upgrade expands 1.8.0, 1.7.0 and 1.6.0; manual visits expand only the current release. The guide also covers resource downloads, masks and previews.

Clearer English and Japanese copy\nReviewed actions, download states, storage and icon terminology against HyperOS system resources. Added translation contribution guidance and resource checks to support future languages.

resources.string: Importing or previewing a mask does not apply a theme. Update or regenerate and apply icons after changing masks or generation options. Special resources retain their own rules, and dynamic previews use static snapshots.
Adopted MIUIX OS4 throughout the app, reorganized Desktop settings, status information and onboarding, and corrected icon corners and pale edges on some dark icons.

string-array.name: release_notes_1_7_0_changes
string-array.item: OS4 interface and two navigation styles\nUpdated buttons, menus, disclosures and glass components with consistent icons and concise labels. Both iOS-like and OS4 Glass bottom navigation remain available.

Grouped Desktop settings\nDock, Appearance, and Icons and launch now have dedicated pages. The overview shows a short launcher version and fault states; status pills follow control order, with pending progress beneath the affected control.
Separate Dock and search materials\nSet Dock materials on its own page. Search can use an independent material or follow Dock, reducing the need to search across pages.

Compact status and icon pack settings\nConnection, sync, failure and interruption states use clear pills. More settings and icon preview preferences now belong to Icon packs, with clearer Monet status, links and toolbar actions.

Visual cache management\nA cylinder chart and categories show storage use and link to resource management. Edit the cleanup reminder threshold; the default is 500 MB or 1 GB depending on downloaded Perfect Icons resources. Resources are not automatically deleted.

Rebuilt scope authorization and onboarding\nThe scope page shows component versions and individual grants. The five-step guide supports resuming, postponing and replaying, distinguishes authorization from loading and effect, and explains linked settings.

Correct default icon corners and pale edges\nMissing native icon configuration is completed by default, improving square fallback icons and pale edges in third-party packs. Existing pack configuration takes priority; completion can be disabled in More settings.
System component compatibility\nAdded structural validation for launcher 8607 and SecurityCenter 13.8.1. Compatibility continues to use actual code and resources rather than version numbers alone.

resources.string: Icon effects depend on resources and system support. Update or regenerate and apply existing schemes to receive configuration fixes. A scope grant does not establish that its process has loaded the module or that a feature has taken effect.
Built for the Rust + Flutter HyperOS system launcher, with dynamic compatibility discovery, API 102 automatic hot reload, and in-app feature and connection status.

string-array.name: release_notes_1_4_0_changes
string-array.item: Automatic light and dark icons\nSupported icons in the built-in Default / Classic / Boundless packs follow the system appearance without importing another icon pack.
Monet themed icons\nEnable Monet colors for supported icons and follow the system appearance. Choose AOSP or ColorOS-inspired color styles, or custom colors.
APK icon packs\nGenerate, import and automatically apply an icon scheme in one action. Get compatibility update reminders or manually update applied icons.
MTZ / ZIP icon imports\nImport compatible third-party MTZ / ZIP icon packs and use their existing light, dark, palette-aware and dynamic resources.
Built-in ColorOS icon schemes\nChoose Classic, Daylight, Night Shadow, Material, Pebble and ART+ redraws with their supported light and dark artwork, plus the Inspiration Monet scheme.

Icon completion and fallback\nTry name matching for system apps missing from a pack and fall back to the selected HyperOS built-in icons. Additional ColorOS fallback resources fill gaps while prioritizing existing app support for light, dark and Monet icons.
Icon previews\nCheck app coverage and support for light, dark and Monet icons, and preview icons and fallbacks under the current scheme.
Native soft-glass Dock\nReuse native glass materials and animations, with an unlock entrance animation, adaptive width for 1–5 apps, and different corner policies.
Long app names\nChoose two-line labels or scrolling long names. Scrolling pauses while organizing the home screen to preserve native drag and selection interactions.
System environment information\nView the device model, system and launcher versions, and the Rust / Flutter runtime information used by the launcher for troubleshooting and feedback.
Preserve system materials\nRestore supported system materials and icon highlights when using third-party packs, while respecting system power-saving and blur settings.
ColorOS-style launch background adaptation at night\nDim light solid-color launch backgrounds when an app is in dark mode, while preserving brand colors, custom launch icons and snapshots.

resources.string: Note: Icon effects depend on the resources supplied by the pack and app. Dynamic and launch-background effects depend on their actual system application. Imported or updated packs must be applied. Some settings take effect after reopening a panel or on the next cold start; see the in-app guidance.

string-array.name: release_notes_1_5_0_changes
string-array.item: Fixed Dock glass disappearing with five apps on launcher 9226 under some DPI and icon-size combinations.
Completed dynamic compatibility for Monet, Dock and related features on launcher 8604, and fixed a listener-retirement race during automatic hot reload.
Added Pad-style Dock corners, a screen-concentric reference and a custom radius, plus height and vertical-position controls.
Improved resource cleanup when opening apps, returning home and dragging across pages or with multiple selections. Corrected edit-mode animation coordination and reduced some main-thread work.
Improved image reuse, packaging and Monet configuration synchronization during icon generation to reduce redundant resources and configuration reads.
Added “Only generate icons for installed apps”, off by default, to optionally reduce the generation scope.

Improved waiting and automatic rechecking for large packs and slow theme operations to reduce false import or application failures. Fixed some source-identification and completion-status refresh issues.
Moved “Icon packs and actions” into a separate Settings page. Standardized update, export and cleanup floating actions, and improved onboarding and large-text layouts.
Improved log filenames with device, system and launcher versions. Clarified that feature issues require LSPosed logs; app logs cover issues within this app only.

resources.string: Added Apple icon schemes and the Perfect Icons Completion Project, expanded icon-pack support across system surfaces, and improved dynamic resources and launcher compatibility.

string-array.name: release_notes_1_6_0_changes
string-array.item: Added Apple icon schemes with iOS, iPadOS or macOS artwork, light and dark appearances, resolution and corner options, local caching, manual and batch matching, and mapping import and export.

Added a Perfect Icons Completion Project page for resource synchronization, style selection, local generation and previews. Downloaded resources can also supply fallback icons for uncovered system apps.

Improved recognition and import of native layers, light and dark variants, and supported dynamic resources in MTZ / ZIP packs. Apple Calendar and Clock can use native dynamic resources; previews remain static snapshots.

Added optional dark adaptation for Perfect Icons Completion Project artwork, covering static layered icons and eligible dynamic layers. Existing independent dark resources take priority, and preview options stay consistent with generation.

Supported recent-task icons, notification app icons, HyperOS system share targets, Settings app management and details, and Security Sidebar icons now follow the current pack, appearance and Monet colors. Security compatibility caches detect APK-content changes to avoid reusing outdated results when version numbers stay the same.

Fixed undersized ColorOS fallback icons for Download Manager and some preinstalled non-system apps. Factory packages and signatures identify eligible native artwork. Added mappings from Themes and Theme Store to the ColorOS Theme Store icon.
Improved Monet integration and light/dark previews for supported APK and MTZ packs. Preserved declared names, versions, authors and designers to reduce unknown names and source-identification errors.

Improved archive reading, nested-resource accounting and raw-entry copying for large packs to reduce repeated decompression, image copying and preview-cache usage. Failed synchronization or generation preserves the last usable resources.

Improved retirement of old listeners, caches and background tasks during API 102 hot reload to reduce cross-process reload failures and missed appearance updates. Older recent-task icons can also refresh within the supported scope.
Improved compatibility with launcher 9239 for Dock, Monet and related features, while retaining native behavior where unsupported.

Recognized Pad devices and actual launcher capabilities, retaining the native Pad Dock. Unsupported phone-specific features show compatibility status rather than applying phone layouts, and saved choices are preserved.

Reduced repetitive guidance and action labels on icon-pack pages, added optional top-bar help, and made Apply, Update and declared author information easier to find. Fixed bottom-navigation jumps and improved large-text layouts.

Improved first-activation, scope-authorization and onboarding guidance, distinguishing authorization, loading and actual feature status. One system restart is recommended after first authorization; later updates normally use automatic hot reload.

resources.string: Icon effects depend on pack resources and system support. Update or regenerate and apply existing schemes to receive resource corrections. New scopes require framework authorization and their processes must load the module. Unsupported surfaces retain native icons.
